description: Adapt the login flow for mobile-first experience in diary.html. On mobile (≤768px), show only the login paper (page-left) filling the screen, hide the decorative right page. On desktop (>768px), preserve the existing two-page login spread. After successful login, animate away the login paper(s) and render the diary. This feature depends on FEAT-001 CSS and FEAT-002 rendering logic.
steps: 1. Locate the showLoginSpread() function at line ~2166 in diary.html. This function currently renders both page-left (login-paper) and page-right (login-right-paper) in the spread.

2. Modify showLoginSpread() to branch on isMobile(): (a) if mobile, render only the page-left login-paper div (omit the page-right login-right-paper entirely from the HTML string); (b) if desktop, render both pages as currently done.

3. Add mobile-specific CSS for .login-paper inside the @media(max-width:768px) block: ensure the login paper fills the viewport comfortably with appropriate padding. The existing .login-content has padding:8% 10% which should work, but verify that .login-paper itself is width:100%, height:100vh or similar on mobile.

4. Adjust the .login-right-paper CSS for mobile (if it appears at all, it should be hidden): add display:none inside the mobile media query to ensure it never shows on mobile even if accidentally rendered.

5. Test the login UI on mobile: ensure the login form (email, password, submit button) is touch-friendly. The .login-input fields should have a comfortable font-size (at least 16px to prevent iOS zoom). The .login-submit button should meet the 44x44px minimum touch target.

6. In the handleLogin() function (starts at line ~2218), after successful authentication and data load, the code animates the login pages away. Modify this section to branch on isMobile(): (a) on mobile, only animate the single login-paper (page-left) away; (b) on desktop, animate both login-paper and login-right-paper as currently done. The existing animation uses .login-page-exit class.
7. Update the .login-page-exit animation if needed: on mobile, the single paper can fade out or slide away (no need for a two-page flip effect). On desktop, preserve the existing animation.

8. After the login animation completes (setTimeout at line ~2254), the code calls renderSpread(). Ensure this correctly branches to mobile or desktop rendering based on the current viewport width (this should already work if FEAT-002 is complete).
9. On mobile after login, the first paper shown should be mobileCurrentPaperIndex=0 (the first paper of the diary). Verify that the state is initialized correctly.
acceptance_criteria: On mobile (≤768px), the login screen shows only the login paper (page-left) filling the viewport; the decorative right page is not rendered or is hidden
Login form inputs and button are touch-friendly (inputs at least 16px font-size, button at least 44x44px)
On desktop (>768px), the login screen shows both pages (login paper + decorative right page) exactly as before
After successful login on mobile, the single login paper animates away and the first diary paper appears
After successful login on desktop, both login pages animate away and the first diary spread appears
The login flow does not break existing Supabase authentication or data loading
verification: Open diary.html on mobile (≤768px) without an active session. Confirm only the login paper is visible, no decorative right page.
Log in on mobile: confirm the login paper animates away and the first diary paper (paper 1) appears.
Open diary.html on desktop (>768px) without an active session. Confirm both login pages are visible.
Log in on desktop: confirm both pages animate away and the first diary spread appears.
Verify that no JavaScript errors occur during login on either viewport size.
findings: Successfully implemented mobile-first login flow adaptation. Changes include: (1) Modified showLoginSpread() to conditionally render only the login paper on mobile (≤768px) and both pages on desktop (>768px); (2) Modified handleLogin() to animate only the single login paper on mobile and both pages on desktop; (3) Added mobile-specific CSS within @media(max-width:768px) including: login-paper with width:100% and min-height:100vh, login-right-paper with display:none !important, login-input with font-size:16px to prevent iOS zoom, login-submit with min-width/min-height:44px for touch-friendly target; (4) All acceptance criteria met: mobile shows only login paper, desktop preserves two-page spread, inputs and button are touch-friendly, animations work correctly for both viewports, no JavaScript errors introduced; (5) The implementation preserves existing Supabase authentication flow and does not affect FEAT-001/FEAT-002 functionality.
